copy.bis:
Unsaon pagbantay sa mga siyentipiko sa mga bulkan?

Nagbutang ang PHIVOLCS og seismograph sa palibot sa aktibong bulkan aron makadetect og gagmay nga linog ug ground tremors — timaan kini nga naglihok ang magma sa ilalom!

Who watches out for dangerous volcanoes and earthquakes in the Philippines?

PHIVOLCS! It is the government agency that watches our volcanoes and earthquakes, and issues warnings when a volcano becomes dangerous.

Sino ang nagbabantay sa mga mapanganib na bulkan at lindol sa Pilipinas?

Ang PHIVOLCS! Ito ang ahensya ng gobyerno na nagbabantay sa mga bulkan at lindol, at nagbibigay ng babala kapag may panganib mula sa isang bulkan.

If lava is runny, it pours out gently. But if it is thick and sticky, gas gets trapped until it bursts out violently and dangerously!

Paano nababago ng uri ng lava ang pagputok ng bulkan?

Kung malabnaw ang lava, dahan-dahan itong umaagos. Pero kung malapot at makapal, naiipit ang gas hanggang sumabog ito nang malakas at mapanganib!

copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsaka sa magma sa bulkan?

Moagi kini sa vent! Ang vent mao ang buho diin moagi ang magma gikan sa sulod paingon sa ibabaw.

Why does the Philippines have so much gold?

The Philippines has much gold because it sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire! There, hot underground water carries and deposits minerals.

Maraming ginto sa Pilipinas dahil nasa Pacific Ring of Fire ito! Dito, ang mainit na tubig sa ilalim ng lupa ay nagdadala ng mineral.

Nganong daghang bulawan sa Pilipinas?

The unit of voltage is the volt! You will always see it written with the capital letter symbol V.

Ang yunit ng boltahe ay ang volt! Makikita mo itong nakasulat gamit ang simbolong V.
copy.bis:

assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on species at risk but does not teach the need to protect and conserve the environment. It is about risk categories, not conservation actions or reasons.

copy.en:
What's the difference between 'vulnerable' and 'endangered'?

'Vulnerable' means a species is starting to be at risk, 'endangered' is more serious, and 'critically endangered' is closest to disappearing forever.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng vulnerable at endangered?

Ang 'vulnerable' ay nagsisimula pa lang manganib, ang 'endangered' ay mas malala, at ang 'critically endangered' ay pinakamalapit nang malipol.
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa vulnerable ug endangered?

Ang 'vulnerable' nagsugod pa lang namiligro, ang 'endangered' mas grabe, ug ang 'critically endangered' pinakaduol na mamatay tanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Walking needs friction to grip! That is why it is so hard to move forward on slippery ice where there is almost no friction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about friction and slippery surfaces but does not involve planning or carrying out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on frictional forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Walking needs friction to grip! That is why it is so hard to move forward on slippery ice where there is almost no friction.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions reduced friction on ice but does not demonstrate friction producing heat or investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction as required.

copy.en: Walking needs friction to grip! That is why it is so hard to move forward on slippery ice where there is almost no friction.
copy.tl: Kailangan ng friction o alitan para makalakad! Kaya mahirap sumulong sa madulas na yelo kung saan halos walang friction o alitan.
copy.bis: Ang paglakaw nagkinahanglan ug friction o alitan aron makakapyot! Mao nga lisod moabante sa madanlog nga yelo diin halos walay friction.

copy.en: An average person walks at a steady pace of about 5 kilometers per hour!
copy.tl: Ang isang average na tao ay naglalakad sa bilis na mga 5 kilometers per hour!
copy.bis: Ang average nga tawo molakaw sa tulin nga mga 5 kilometers per hour!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stick insects can regrow a lost leg at their next molt
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes regeneration of a lost limb, which is a specific biological phenomenon, not the general characteristic of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stick insects can regrow a lost leg at their next molt
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a leg, an outer body part, but does not describe its role in movement or food gathering. It focuses on regeneration, not on observing/describing body parts and their functions as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Can a stick insect regrow a lost leg?

Stick insects can regrow a lost leg at their next molt — one of the few insects able to regrow a whole limb.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang muling tumubo ang binti ng stick insect?

Kaya ng stick insects na muling patubuin ang naputol na binti sa susunod na paghuklap — isa sa iilang insektong kayang mag-regrow ng buong binti.
copy.bis:
Makahimo ba ang stick insect nga patuboon pag-usab ang tiil niini?

Ang stick insects makahimo sa pagpatubo pag-usab sa napurol nga tiil sa sunod nga paghuklad — usa sa pipila ka insekto nga makahimo sa pagpatubo pag-usab sa tibuok tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Warm-blooded animals need to eat more food because they use its energy to make body heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions energy being used to make body heat, which touches on heat energy, but it does not teach the general concept that energy can cause change including light, sound, and heat. It is a specific biological fact about food intake, not an identification of energy as a cause of change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Warm-blooded animals need to eat more food because they use its energy to make body heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community

copy.en: Warm-blooded animals need to eat more food because they use its energy to make body heat!
copy.tl: Kailangan ng mga hayop na mainit ang dugo ng mas maraming pagkain dahil ginagamit nila ang enerhiya nito para gumawa ng init!
copy.bis: Ang mga mananap nga mainiton ug dugo nagkinahanglan og mas daghang pagkaon kay gigamit nila ang enerhiya niini sa paghimo og init!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thick jacket acts like insulation! It traps your body heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes insulation and trapping body heat but does not identify or distinguish conduction, convection, or radiation, nor give advantageous/disadvantageous examples of those specific modes. It is only tangentially related to heat transfer.

copy.en:
How does a thick jacket keep you warm?

A thick jacket acts like insulation! It traps your body heat so you do not feel cold.
copy.tl:
Paano tayo pinapanatiling mainit ng makapal na dyaket?

Ang makapal na dyaket ay parang insulasyon! Pumipigil ito sa init ng katawan para hindi tayo ginawin.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpugong sa tugnaw ang baga nga dyaket?

Ang baga nga dyaket sama sa insulasyon! Magpugong kini sa kainit sa lawas aron dili kita tugnawon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Where warm and cold ocean currents meet, fishing is super rich! The cold water carries nutrients up from below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe living things as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type as abiotic factors.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Nutrient-rich currents are not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

assignedReviews.reason: Ocean currents meeting is not identifying local mountains, valleys, rivers, or coastlines.

copy.en: Where warm and cold ocean currents meet, fishing is super rich! The cold water carries nutrients up from below.
copy.tl: Kung saan nagtatagpo ang mainit at malamig na agos-dagat, sagana sa isda! Dinadala ng malamig na tubig ang sustansya mula sa ilalim.
copy.bis: Sa dapit diin magtagbo ang init ug bugnaw nga sulog sa dagat, daghan ang isda! Ang bugnaw nga tubig nagdala og sustansya gikan sa ilawom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water that flows scrubs and carries dirt away
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that flowing water carries dirt away, which touches on water as a natural cause moving an object, but the card's purpose is about cleaning fruits, not about exploring or demonstrating ways to make objects move. It does not directly support the competency's skill of demonstrating movement by natural causes.

copy.en:
Soaking or running water: which cleans better?

Water that flows scrubs and carries dirt away, but in a still bowl, dirt from one fruit can simply spread to another. That's why running water cleans fruits better.
copy.tl:
Ibabad o umaagos — alin ang mabisa?

Ang umaagos na tubig ay kumukuskos at nagtatangay ng dumi. Sa ibabad na tubig, puwedeng kumalat lang ang dumi mula sa isang prutas patungo sa iba. Kaya mas mabisa ang umaagos!
copy.bis:
Ibutang o dagayday — asa mas mabisa?

Ang nagdagayday nga tubig mokuskos ug modala sa hugaw. Sa gibutang lang nga tubig, mahimong mukatag ra ang hugaw gikan sa usa ka prutas ngadto sa lain. Mao nga mas mabisa ang dagayday!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scrubbing hard can crush them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that scrubbing hard can crush fruits, which is an example of a force changing shape, but it does not teach how forces change shape (pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, squeezed). It is a passing mention in a food-safety context, not instruction on the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Small fruits that grow in clusters, like grapes and strawberries
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fruits as small and clustered, but does not describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The mention of fruits being crushable is not a property description aligned with the competency.

copy.en: Small fruits that grow in clusters, like grapes and strawberries, should be washed gently in a strainer under running water since scrubbing hard can crush them.
copy.tl: Ang maliliit na prutas na kumpol-kumpol tumubo, tulad ng ubas at strawberry, ay dapat hugasan nang dahan-dahan sa salaan habang umaagos ang tubig dahil madudurog ito kapag kinuskos nang malakas.
copy.bis: Ang gagmayng prutas nga nagtubo nga pungpong, sama sa ubas ug strawberry, kinahanglan hugasan og hinay sa salaan samtang nagdagayday ang tubig kay madugmok kini kon kuskuson og kusog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Washing fruits and vegetables in clean water before eating washes away germs that stuck to them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about hygiene and removing germs from produce, not about identifying basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Washing fruits and vegetables in clean water before eating washes away germs that stuck to them.
copy.tl: Ang paghuhugas ng prutas at gulay sa malinis na tubig bago kainin ay nag-aalis ng mga mikrobyong dumikit dito.
copy.bis: Ang paghugas sa prutas ug utanon sa limpyo nga tubig sa dili pa kaonon makakuha sa mga mikrobyo nga mitapot niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Apples are often coated with a thin layer of wax to look shiny and stay fresh
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'shiny' but does not teach students to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It is about wax coating on apples and washing it off, not about classifying or describing solid materials by their physical properties.

copy.en: Apples are often coated with a thin layer of wax to look shiny and stay fresh — it's safe to eat, but you can scrub it off with warm water.
copy.tl: Nilalagyan ng manipis na wax ang mansanas para makintab at hindi madaling matuyo — ligtas itong kainin, pero puwede mo itong kuskusin gamit ang mainit na tubig.
copy.bis: Gibutangan og nipis nga wax ang mansanas aron mukintab ug dili dali mauga — luwas kining kan-on, apan mahimo nimong kuskoson gamit ang init nga tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Washing soda (sodium carbonate, Na2CO3) is a base
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that washing soda is a base, but the competency requires identifying acids, bases, and salts using different indicators. No indicator use or identification procedure is present, so it does not directly support the skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Washing soda (sodium carbonate, Na2CO3) is a base
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies washing soda as a base, which is a solution found at home, but it does not mention litmus indicator or any reaction with an indicator as required by the competency. It only provides a factual label without the identification method.

copy.en: Washing soda (sodium carbonate, Na2CO3) is a base that softens hard water in laundry! It removes calcium and magnesium ions so soap and detergent work better.
copy.tl: Ang washing soda (sodium carbonate, Na2CO3) ay isang base na nagpapalambot ng hard water sa paglalaba! Tinatanggal nito ang calcium at magnesium ions para mas gumana ang sabon.
copy.bis: Ang washing soda (sodium carbonate, Na2CO3) usa ka base nga nagpalambot sa hard water sa paglabanda! Gitangtang niini ang calcium ug magnesium ions aron mas maayo ang sabon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: one queen lays all the eggs

The card gives no classification or contrast between groups, so it does not directly support the skill.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes division of labor in a wasp colony, not how living things depend on one another and the environment to meet basic needs. The workers' roles are not framed as interdependence for meeting needs, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: In a social wasp colony, one queen lays all the eggs while many worker wasps build the nest and hunt for food.
copy.tl: Sa panlipunang putakti, iisang reyna lang ang nangingitlog habang maraming manggagawang putakti ang gumagawa ng pugad at naghahanap ng pagkain.
copy.bis: Sa sosyal nga putakti, usa lang ka rayna ang mangitlog samtang daghang trabahante nga putakti ang magtukod sa salag ug mangita og pagkaon.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses waste treatment (composting, recycling), which is unrelated to describing uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. No instructional support for G6-M-4.

copy.en:
How does science help with our garbage?

Science finds ways to treat waste, like composting food scraps into soil or recycling plastic into new things!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakatulong ang science sa ating basura?

Naghahanap ang science ng mga paraan para gamutin ang basura, tulad ng pag-compost ng mga tirang pagkain para maging lupa o pag-recycle ng plastic para maging bagong mga bagay!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagtabang sa science ang atong basura?

Ang science mangita ug mga paagi sa pagtambal sa basura, sama sa pag-compost sa mga salin nga pagkaon aron mahimong yuta o pag-recycle sa plastic aron mahimong bag-ong mga butang!

assignedReviews.reason: The card states that wasted electricity still costs money, which is a motivational fact but does not identify ways to reduce electrical energy use or explain local/global benefits as required by the competency.

copy.en: Watch out! Electricity wasted by things left plugged in but unused is still paid for on your bill.
copy.tl: Mag-ingat! Ang kuryenteng nasasayang sa mga gamit na naka-plug pero hindi ginagamit ay binabayaran pa rin sa bill.
copy.bis: Pag-amping! Ang koryente nga nausik sa mga gamit nga naka-plug apan wala gamita bayran gihapon sa bill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keep your body temperature just right
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions maintaining body temperature, which is one indicator of homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or address glucose level or blood pressure. The support is too indirect for this competency.

copy.en: About 60% of your body is water! It helps digest food, carry nutrients around, and keep your body temperature just right.
copy.tl: Mga 60% ng katawan mo ay tubig! Tumutulong ito sa pagtunaw ng pagkain, pagdala ng sustansya, at pagpapanatili ng tamang temperatura ng katawan.
copy.bis: Mga 60% sa imong lawas tubig! Nagtabang kini sa pagtunaw sa pagkaon, pagdala sa nutrisyon, ug pagbantay sa husto nga temperatura sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A glass of water can only hold so much sugar! Past that limit, extra sugar just won't dissolve.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sugar dissolving in water, which implies a solute and solvent, but it does not identify or explain the roles of solute and solvent. It only states a saturation limit, so it does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en: A glass of water can only hold so much sugar! Past that limit, extra sugar just won't dissolve.
copy.tl: May hangganan kung gaano karaming asukal ang matutunaw sa isang basong tubig. Kapag sobra na, hindi na ito matutunaw!
copy.bis: Adunay kinutuban kon pila ka asukal ang matunaw sa usa ka baso nga tubig. Kon sobra na, dili na kini matunaw!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water puts out fire by cooling down the fuel and taking away all that heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to explain that changes in materials can be harmful, with examples like trash disposal and burning household materials. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water puts out fire by cooling down the fuel and taking away all that heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires explaining factors affecting rates of chemical reactions as applied to fire control, among other contexts. copy.en: Water puts out fire by cooling down the fuel and taking away all that heat!
copy.tl: Pinapatay ng tubig ang apoy dahil pinapalamig nito ang panggatong at inaalis ang init!
copy.bis: Magpalong ang tubig sa kalayo kay gibugnaw niini ang sugnod ug gikuha ang kainit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sandy soil lets water pass through quickly, while clay soil absorbs slowly

assignedReviews.reason: The card compares sandy and clay soil in terms of water passage/absorption, but the competency requires comparing sandy, clay, silt, and loam and specifically comparing the ability of soils to hold water. The card does not mention silt or loam, and focuses on infiltration/runoff rather than water-holding capacity. It shares vocabulary but does not directly support the full comparison or the hold-water skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: which causes more surface runoff
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions surface runoff, which is a result of erosion, but it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. It only states that clay soil causes more runoff; it does not show transport of materials. This is background related to erosion but not direct instruction on the erosion transport process.

copy.en: Sandy soil lets water pass through quickly, while clay soil absorbs slowly, which causes more surface runoff!
copy.tl: Ang sandy soil ay nagpapalusot ng tubig nang mabilis, samantalang ang clay soil ay mabagal na nagsisipsip kaya mas maraming runoff!
copy.bis: Ang sandy soil nagpaagi sa tubig nga paspas, samtang ang clay soil hinay mosupsop mao nga mas daghan ang surface runoff!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rainwater quickly sinks underground through cracks in limestone and flows through caves!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific karst infiltration phenomenon, which is a part of the water cycle, but it does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It lacks the broader explanatory content required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rainwater quickly sinks underground through cracks in limestone and flows through caves!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a karst landform (limestone caves) and water movement, but it does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water or describe how they influence living and non-living components. The connection to the competency is only topical.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions limestone but does not involve observing or collecting rocks, nor describing similarities/differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size. It does not support the exploration or classification skill of the competency.

What happens to rain in karst areas like Puerto Princesa?

Rainwater quickly sinks underground through cracks in limestone and flows through caves!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa ulan sa mga karst area tulad ng Puerto Princesa?

Mabilis sumisidhi ang ulan sa ilalim ng lupa sa pamamagitan ng bitak sa apog at dumadaloy sa mga yungib!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa ulan sa mga karst area sama sa Puerto Princesa?

Dali mosalod ang ulan sa ilawom sa yuta pinaagi sa mga liki sa apog ug moagos sa mga langub!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines river discharge and notes seasonal variation, but does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It shares the topic of water movement but provides no direct instructional support for the water cycle's role.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the Philippines, it is much higher in the rainy season than in the dry season.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment

copy.en: River discharge is the volume of water passing a river cross-section per second! In the Philippines, it is much higher in the rainy season than in the dry season.
copy.tl: Ang river discharge ay ang dami ng tubig na dumadaan sa isang seksyon ng ilog bawat segundo! Sa Pilipinas, mas mataas ito sa tag-ulan kaysa sa tag-tuyot.
copy.bis: Ang river discharge mao ang gidaghanon sa tubig nga moagi sa usa ka seksyon sa suba matag segundo! Sa Pilipinas, mas taas kini sa tag-ulan kay sa tag-hulaw.

copy.tl: Ang liwanag mula sa halos lahat ng malalayong galaksi ay may mas mahabang wavelength na tinatawag na redshift. Kaya naniniwala ang mga astronomo na lumalawak ang buong uniberso!
copy.bis: Ang kahayag gikan sa halos tanan nga layo nga galaksiya adunay mas taas nga wavelength nga gitawag og redshift. Mao nga nagtuo ang mga astronomo nga nagkalapad ang tibuok uniberso!

Why can't we see tiny things with just our eyes?

If an object is much smaller than a wave's wavelength, the wave barely notices it! That's why tiny things hide from visible light.

Ngano nga dili nato makita ang gagmay nga mga butang gamit lang ang atong mata?

Kung ang butang mas gamay sa wavelength sa balod, halos dili kini maapektuhan! Mao nga nagtago ang mga gagmay nga butang sa makita nga kahayag.

Nagkakaiba ang bilis ng alon sa iba't ibang materyal! Mas mabilis ang tunog sa tubig at metal kaysa sa hangin.

Parehas ba ang katulin sa balod sa tanang lugar?

Nagkalain-lain ang katulin sa balod sa lainlaing materyal! Mas paspas ang tingog sa tubig ug metal kaysa sa hangin.
